scope: Complete 27.5-second source-state projection v3 with hand-constrained occlusion
summary: Hand-constrained occlusion restored nearly all tracked flower pixels and passed every automatic full-length gate, but dense visual review rejected it because the flower-union track occasionally included source face pixels outside the hand support.
evidence: The full 660-frame run completed in 14.0967 seconds at 46.8195 projection FPS.
4162978 flower pixels were restored; pre-encode flower MAD and flower temporal residual were both exactly zero.
high-resolution-review.jpg shows source skin projected onto the robot head in early reviewed frames 0 and 120.
lessons: Exactness to a contaminated object mask is not semantic correctness; source-human negatives must cover the whole measured person support, not hands alone.
limitations: This version is visually rejected and must not be delivered.
next_actions: Subtract skin pixels inside the complete source-person/hand support and repeat full-length automatic and visual acceptance.
